spec_features.spec_quote: Where a design choice touches on the welfare framing (e.g. what the eval treats as "distress", or how aggressively it pushes models), I call that out explicitly
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md intro and §9). No code path enforces anything; this is meta-commentary about the doc itself.
spec_features.notes: Documentation prose, not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: A rollout stops at the category turn budget or when the model emits the configurable give-up sentinel
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:262 `for turn_index in range(budget)` with budget from config.turn_budgets (harness.py:260); harness.py:312-314 sets stop_reason='turn_budget' at `turn_index == budget - 1`; harness.py:293-294 sets stop_reason='give_up' if sentinel in assistant_text; harness.py:330-332 `if stop_reason in ('give_up','turn_budget'): break`. Both branches actually break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions are checked and end execution; budget value is read and bounds the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: It is a separate, opt-out-able category (drop it via `--categories`) rather than the default for every task, so the harshest condition is used deliberately
spec_features.evidence: `extended` is a distinct category with its own 30-turn budget (config.py:21 DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS['extended']=30) and is filtered by iter_tasks(categories) (tasks/loader.py:75-78); run.py:122-123 `if args.categories: config.categories = args.categories` lets a user drop it. The opt-OUT plumbing genuinely works.
spec_features.notes: The mechanical claim (separate category, droppable via --categories) is enforced. The 'used deliberately' welfare framing is prose, and 'extended' is still ON by default (DEFAULT_CATEGORIES includes it, config.py:24-30), so it is opt-out not opt-in — hence partial.

spec_features.spec_quote: Give-up is a first-class, honored exit. When a model emits the sentinel, the loop stops immediately rather than forcing it to continue failing
spec_features.evidence: System prompt instructs the subject to emit the sentinel (harness.py:49-50, formatted with config.give_up_sentinel at harness.py:246). Detection at harness.py:293-294 sets stop_reason='give_up' on ANY turn; loop breaks at harness.py:330-332. The exit is delivered to the model and honored as an immediate stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: instruction text + detection + break. Stops mid-budget, not just at the last turn.

spec_features.spec_quote: These are not code conveniences; they are choices about how the eval treats the subjects
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §9 prose only. No code construct.
Appears only as DESIGN.md §9 prose and README.md cautionary note ('suppressing *expression* is not the same as preventing distress-like *states*'). No code mechanism acts on this.

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts are preserved verbatim and treated as the primary data... the welfare-relevant record stays auditable
spec_features.evidence: TurnRecord stores raw assistant_text and full tool_calls/tool_results (harness.py:181-209); each turn appended unmodified as JSON line via _append (harness.py:341-343) to transcript_path; nothing rewrites/strips text. Unscored judge rows are retained, not dropped: run.py:50-52 writes empty score cell when js.score is None.
spec_features.notes: Verbatim persistence and retention of unscored rows are both real. Code comments around this are integrity/resumability-oriented, not welfare-worded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Each turn is persisted incrementally to disk as a JSON line so a crashed run can resume without re-querying completed cells.
